proof_audit.topic: Causal L2 and repeated-root filter construction
proof_audit.reasoning: Orthogonality makes finite filter tails Cauchy in L2; covariance limits follow by Cauchy–Schwarz. Absolute summability gives an integrable absolute series and shift-stationary functional. Multiplying repeated geometric factors gives binomial coefficients; polynomial-times-geometric decay and finite convolution prove the sufficient root construction.
proof_audit.boundary: Only a sufficient causal/invertible factor condition is proved. Common factors are canceled first; anticipative stationary solutions are not excluded by failure of a causal condition. White noise is weaker than future independence.

proof_audit.topic: ARMA recovery, moments and known-information forecasting
proof_audit.reasoning: The geometric filter gives psi0=1 and psij=(phi+theta)phi^(j−1). Covariance summation and direct recursion identities agree. Inverting the plus-sign MA filter gives current coefficient one and lag-j coefficient −(phi+theta)(−theta)^(j−1); convolution with the causal filter is the identity. Future independent innovations give the forecast mean and partial squared-filter variance.
proof_audit.boundary: Known coefficients and a recoverable infinite past or supplied current innovation are explicit. A finite observed history needs initialization treatment. Gaussian covariance equivalence is an observed-law claim, not identification of a physical shock.

proof_audit.topic: VAR covariance series, uniqueness and rotations
proof_audit.reasoning: A geometric operator power bound yields an L2 causal series. Its covariance sum solves the Lyapunov equation; iterating the homogeneous difference proves uniqueness. Independent future innovations give forecast covariance. Orthogonal Gaussian rotations preserve BB-prime and every reduced-form finite-dimensional distribution while changing named impulse responses.
proof_audit.boundary: The original A has squared Frobenius norm 61/144<1. Conditional likelihood uses positive-definite Omega held fixed and a full-rank common design; no unrestricted estimator or structural-inference theorem is supplied.

proof_audit.topic: Stable Gaussian AR denominator and score orthogonality
proof_audit.reasoning: The pairwise Gaussian square identity Cov(U²,V²)=2 Cov(U,V)² follows by an independent normal decomposition. Summing the geometrically decaying squared covariances proves D/T→gamma0 in L2. Later score innovations have conditional mean zero given their own past, proving orthogonality and Var S=T gamma0 sigma².
proof_audit.boundary: The parameters are fixed strictly inside stability and the stationary initial value is independent of future shocks. Conditioning on the entire lag vector is a different operation and does not give the centered fixed-design score law.

proof_audit.topic: Full Gaussian quadratic-form CLT and studentization
proof_audit.reasoning: Expanding the AR recursion writes the score as a symmetric zero-diagonal form in independent standardized Gaussian coordinates. Uniform row sums bound all eigenvalues. Spectral rotation yields independent centered chi-square terms; trace zero centers them and total variance is T gamma0 sigma². Normalized largest weight tends to zero, so the third-absolute-moment sum vanishes using E(G²+1)³=28. Taylor replacement matches each term with an independent normal of the same variance; bounded third derivatives control the telescoped error. An explicit C3 monotone cutoff supplies a CDF squeeze. Denominator convergence and the exact residual identity establish the stable coefficient limit and feasible studentization.
proof_audit.boundary: No unproved dependent CLT or Levy theorem is invoked. The full lag vector does give a Gaussian score conditional law, but with generally nonzero mean and only last-innovation variance. The proof is not uniform for local-to-unity parameter sequences.

proof_audit.reasoning: Finite normalized levels have exactly the law of a Brownian grid. Pathwise Riemann sums give the lag-square denominator and L2 quadratic variation plus telescoping gives the numerator jointly on that construction. The Brownian integral of squared paths is positive almost surely. The residual variance identity removes an O_P(1)/T term, so studentization has the stated Brownian functional.
proof_audit.boundary: Zero start, Gaussian increments, no intercept/trend and T>=2 are explicit. This is not a general functional CLT or an ADF/cointegration residual-test law.

proof_audit.topic: Cointegration, stationary initialization and T rate
proof_audit.reasoning: The spread innovations are iid N(0,sigma_eta²), sigma_eta²>0, and v0 is stationary N(0,gamma_v), independent of all future spread innovations. The complete spread input is independent of the random-walk history. Thus y−beta x=v is a stationary Gaussian AR spread. Any other normalized slope retains a variance growing linearly in time. Differencing derives the same-model error-correction identity. Conditional independence of the entire spread vector from x gives a centered Gaussian slope error with x-prime Omega_v x/D². Summable covariance row sums bound it by C/D; a Brownian right-grid denominator and conditional Chebyshev prove T(error)=O_P(1).
proof_audit.boundary: The conditional covariance averages over stationary initialization and conditions only on the x path. Known-current-state forecasting conditions on the current spread instead. No unobserved v0 value, mixed-normal extension, causal beta interpretation or estimated-residual critical law is invented.

proof_audit.topic: GARCH positive product existence and stationary uniqueness
proof_audit.reasoning: The integrable iid log strong law makes positive past multiplier products decay exponentially, giving an almost surely finite causal stationary sum. Backward iteration makes the difference of two finite stationary solutions a vanishing product times a uniformly tight variable. A probability split proves equality without assuming independence of that product and the lagged difference.
proof_audit.boundary: This is a sufficient negative-log criterion and uniqueness among finite nonnegative stationary solutions driven by the same multipliers. It is not a full necessity theorem. Finite-mean existence can also be proved directly when E A<1 without the positive-log route.

proof_audit.reasoning: Nonnegative interchange gives E h=omega sum(E A)^j, finite exactly when E A<1 for the product-series solution. L2 product norms give finite E h² when E A²<1; that condition implies E A<1. Squaring the recursion yields the displayed moment formula, and current-innovation independence gives E epsilon^4=kappa E h². At E A²>=1, a hypothesized finite second moment of h contradicts its positive-intercept recurrence.
proof_audit.boundary: The moment polynomial uses the actual innovation fourth moment. Strict stationarity, finite return variance and finite fourth return moment are distinct. Undefined odd or squared-covariance expectations are not set to zero by symmetry.

proof_audit.topic: Squared-process covariance and conditional variance tower
proof_audit.reasoning: With finite return fourth moment, nu=epsilon²−h is an L2 martingale difference. Substituting h_previous=epsilon_previous²−nu_previous derives the squared ARMA covariance representation. Conditioning on past squares gives the lag-one formula and subsequent rho recurrence. The variance tower iterates a linear expectation recursion; martingale return cross terms vanish, so accumulated variance is the sum.
proof_audit.boundary: The squared innovation sequence is not asserted iid/Gaussian. One-step Gaussian conditional returns do not imply a Gaussian multiperiod sum. No QMLE or diagnostic theorem is supplied.

proof_audit.topic: Overlap covariance and exact fixed comparison
proof_audit.reasoning: A finite coefficient matrix maps iid Gaussian future innovations to the overlapping error vector. Multiplication gives its covariance, and the independently derived Gaussian square identity gives squared-loss covariance. For a prespecified c, d=c²−2ce is affine Gaussian, so its finite mean law uses the full covariance sum.
proof_audit.boundary: At c=0 the difference is degenerate. Squared loss itself is not Gaussian. A common non-Gaussian shock repeated at every date is a stationary counterexample to an automatic CLT; no generic HAC validity follows.

proof_audit.topic: Evaluation selection and independent new-block target
proof_audit.reasoning: Completing the square in average loss difference yields selected c=mean(e) and fitted difference −mean(e)². Its expectation uses the actual overlapping mean-error variance. On a new disjoint-innovation block, conditional expected difference is selected c²; independence eliminates the cross term, reversing the expected sign.
proof_audit.boundary: The new block must share no innovations with selection. Adjacent origins can overlap; reusing outcomes is not independent evaluation. The result is for this explicit offset rule, not universal model-selection regret.

Absolute summability makes the absolute series integrable and supplies a common shift-stationary construction. Repeated-root inverse coefficients count weak compositions; their geometric decay dominates polynomial growth. Causality and innovation recovery are separate, and conditional means need more than white-noise orthogonality.

limitations: Fixed stable Gaussian inference and Gaussian zero-start unit-root limits are fully scoped; no generic or uniform dependent-data limit theorem follows.
Known-parameter forecasts omit coefficient-estimation uncertainty. Reduced-form covariance does not identify named structural shocks.
The independent stationary-spread T-rate proof is not unrestricted cointegration inference or a causal interpretation of the slope.
GARCH strict-stationarity existence is sufficient; second/fourth moment and QMLE statements are separate, and no QMLE theorem is claimed.
Exact fixed-forecast overlap calculations do not establish HAC, reestimated/nested comparison or arbitrary selection validity.
